title: Thermal Processing, Pasteurisation and Canning
shortDescription: Heat-processing kinetics, blanching, pasteurisation and the canning sequence including process validation.
genZNote: Heat does the killing, kinetics decide how much. D, z, F0 are the receipts for every canned food on the shelf.

sections.heading: Thermal Death Kinetics
bullets: D-value: time at a given temperature for 90% reduction; z-value: temperature rise to reduce D tenfold; F-value: equivalent time at reference temperature (F0 at 121.1 °C, z = 10 °C for low-acid foods).
Botulinum cook: 12D reduction of C. botulinum spores (about F0 ≈ 3 min minimum); spoilage organisms often require higher F0.
Heat penetration: conduction (solid foods), convection (liquids); cold-spot determination, come-up time, headspace and can size influence process time.

sections.heading: Pasteurisation and Blanching
bullets: Pasteurisation targets vegetative pathogens and enzymes: milk 63 °C/30 min or 72 °C/15 s; juices 85–95 °C hot fill for acid foods; eggs and others per standards.
Blanching: 70–100 °C steam/hot water for 1–10 min to inactivate peroxidase/catalase, remove air, soften tissue and fix colour before canning/freezing.

steps.name: Filling and exhausting
steps.explanation: Fill with brine/syrup leaving headspace; exhaust to remove air and form vacuum.

steps.name: Retorting
steps.explanation: Low-acid foods: pressure at ~115–121 °C; acid foods (pH ≤ 4.6): boiling water.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Thermal processing uses controlled heat–time combinations, validated by D, z and F values, to inactivate microbes and enzymes and give safe, shelf-stable foods.

commonTraps: Do not assume canned = sterile of all spores in acid food; they rely on acid.
